title: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act notice requirement
requirement: Before ending a tenancy, a Boston landlord must deliver a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or notice of non-renewal, and send a copy to the Office of Housing Stability.
coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords and foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston; exempt are residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance-abuse treatment facilities.

applicability.per_tenancy: Duty applies when a landlord serves a Notice to Quit or decides not to renew a lease, or a foreclosing owner ends post-foreclosure occupancy.
coverage_quotes: The Ordinance applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.

exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
penalty: Violations are investigated by FHE and enforced by ISD; 1st offense a warning, 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day.
quoted_span: The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement.
